overviewHtml:
Pods that hang while terminating block rollouts and need someone to notice and clean them up manually.

What you get

  • A trigger on the Dynatrace event for pods stuck in the terminating phase
  • Force-deletion through the Kubernetes Automation connector and EdgeConnect
  • Kubernetes manifests for the secret, role, service account and EdgeConnect
  • A test pod to simulate the problem
prereqsHtml:
• Dynatrace SaaS with Workflows and the Kubernetes app
  • Kubernetes cluster monitored by the Dynatrace Operator
  • Kubernetes Automation with EdgeConnect (the dynatrace.kubernetes.connector app)
  • An OAuth client for EdgeConnect
  • kubectl access to the cluster
setupHtml:
1. Set up Kubernetes Automation with the Operator. Follow the operator-supported setup and apply each manifest with kubectl apply -f .yaml:
  • secret.yaml: stores the OAuth client for EdgeConnect.
  • role.yaml: the permissions for the automation use cases.
  • serviceaccount.yaml: the service account that EdgeConnect impersonates to call the Kubernetes API server.
  • rolebinding.yaml: links the service account to the role.
  • edgeconnect.yaml: deploys EdgeConnect in the dynatrace namespace and creates the Kubernetes connection in Dynatrace.
  1. Turn on anomaly detection. In Settings > Anomaly Detection > Workloads, enable detection of pods stuck in the pending and terminating phases (details).
  2. Import the workflow. In Workflows, choose Upload and select kubernetes-stuck-pod-cleanup.workflow-template.yaml. Select the connection that you created with edgeconnect.yaml, then activate the trigger.
  3. Optional: simulate the problem. Apply podtermination.yaml to create a pod that stays in the terminating phase once deleted, then run kubectl delete pods pod-stuck. If your security rules require it, replace the image with one you trust.
  4. Watch it work. Open the Kubernetes app, select Pods and filter for your test cluster. After the detection timeframe (10 minutes by default), the workflow runs and force-deletes the pod.
getStartedHtml:
You need a Kubernetes cluster monitored by the Dynatrace Operator and an OAuth client for EdgeConnect.

  1. Set up Kubernetes Automation with the provided manifests
  2. Enable anomaly detection for stuck pods
  3. Import the workflow and select the connection
  4. Optionally simulate a stuck pod to test
